title: Checks for blocks which are nested beyond a certain threshold.
summary: It can severely hinder readability. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for float literals with a precision greater than that supported by the underlying type.
summary: Rust will truncate the literal silently. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Warns on any exported enums that are not tagged #[non_exhaustive]
summary: Making an enum exhaustive is a stability commitment: adding a variant is a breaking change. A project may wish to ensure that there are no exhaustive enums or that every exhaustive enum is explicitly #[allow]ed. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Warns on any exported structs that are not tagged #[non_exhaustive]
summary: Making a struct exhaustive is a stability commitment: adding a field is a breaking change. A project may wish to ensure that there are no exhaustive structs or that every exhaustive struct is explicitly #[allow]ed. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Detects calls to the exit() function that are not in the main function.
summary: Calls to exit() immediately terminate the program. exit() immediately terminates the program with no information other than an exit code. This provides no means to troubleshoot a problem, and may be an unexpected side effect. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for calls to .expect(&format!(...)), .expect(foo(..)), etc., and suggests to use unwrap_or_else instead
summary: The function will always be called. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for .expect() or .expect_err() calls on Results and .expect() call on Options.
summary: Usually it is better to handle the None or Err case. Still, for a lot of quick-and-dirty code, expect is a good choice, which is why this lint is Allow by default. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for explicit Clone implementations for Copy types.
summary: To avoid surprising behavior, these traits should agree and the behavior of Copy cannot be overridden. In almost all situations a Copy type should have a Clone implementation that does nothing more than copy the object, which is what #[derive(Copy, Clone)] gets you. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for dereferencing expressions which would be covered by auto-deref.
summary: This unnecessarily complicates the code. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for loops over slices with an explicit counter and suggests the use of .enumerate().
summary: Using .enumerate() makes the intent more clear, declutters the code and may be faster in some instances. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for explicit deref() or deref_mut() method calls.
summary: Dereferencing by &*x or &mut *x is clearer and more concise, when not part of a method chain. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for loops on y.into_iter() where y will do, and suggests the latter.
summary: Readability. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for loops on x.iter() where &x will do, and suggests the latter.
summary: Readability. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of write!() / writeln()! which can be replaced with (e)print!() / (e)println!()
summary: Using (e)println! is clearer and more concise Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Nothing.
summary: This lint has been deprecated Clippy puts this lint in the deprecated group, at the level none.

title: Checks for occurrences where one vector gets extended instead of append
summary: Using append instead of extend is more concise and faster Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for lifetimes in generics that are never used anywhere else.
summary: The additional lifetimes make the code look more complicated, while there is nothing out of the ordinary going on. Removing them leads to more readable code. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for type parameters in generics that are never used anywhere else.
summary: Functions cannot infer the value of unused type parameters; therefore, calling them requires using a turbofish, which serves no purpose but to satisfy the compiler. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.
